solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go wrong making lager thus?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: make a careless mistake
second meaning, read as an instruction: the first word written upwards in this down light becomes PILS, a lager

explanation.surface: A brewer wonders whether a mistake is how lager gets made.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: its first word, written up the grid, spells PILS, short for Pilsner lager.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder or make a careless error is to go wrong; the phrasal verb is a common idiom.

clue.text: European celebrity's guiding light?

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A famous European is held up as an inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the north star, has long guided navigators, and the word is used figuratively for any guiding principle.

clue.text: Reno agent I arranged for production

indicators.note: things arranged are set out in a new order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A talent agent in Reno has set things up for a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Generation means the act of producing something, as in the generation of electricity.

clue.text: They carry one some distance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the parts of the body that bear a person along
second meaning: a measure of length, twelve inches each

explanation.surface: Something bears a person over a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Your lower extremities carry you when walking, and the same plural is an imperial unit for measuring length.

clue.text: Cut charge for over-18s possessing ecstasy

indicators.note: possessing means holding something within, so one item sits inside the other

parts.note: the price grown-ups pay, as opposed to a child fare
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An adults-only charge is reduced for those caught with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb about reducing the charge, but it is the definition: drugs are cut by mixing in cheaper stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a substance is to dilute or debase it with inferior additives, which is exactly to adulterate it.

clue.text: English banker not much good?

parts.note: O is nought, as near nothing as can be
as in 'what good is it?', meaning what use is it

explanation.surface: An English bank clerk is judged fairly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks. The OUSE is a river in Yorkshire (another flows through Sussex).
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks on either side, so crosswords call one a banker; this one flows through England.

clue.text: Delivered the support king needs, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to a word heard rather than read

parts.note: a monarch sits on a throne

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether the king's required support has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball delivered by a bowler is thrown or bowled, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that has been pitched or hurled toward a batter has been delivered.

clue.text: Royal correspondents besieging popular courtesan at first

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so one part wraps round the rest
at first points to only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Reporters crowd around a royal mistress, a tabloid picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, so a royal is one example.

clue.text: Promiscuous teacher, one with arm round hooker?

parts.note: loose in the old sense of sexually immoral
a head teacher, the person in charge of a school

explanation.surface: A scandal about a schoolteacher seen embracing a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the hooker is the front-row forward in the middle of the scrum; the loosehead prop binds with an arm round the hooker.
explanation.definitionFit: In a rugby scrum the loosehead prop packs down beside the hooker, binding an arm around that player.

clue.text: Doorkeeper showing drug dealer quietly out

indicators.note: out tells us something is removed and left behind

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: A bouncer discreetly throws a drug dealer out of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people in and guards a door, so the official title once meant a doorkeeper.

clue.text: Administrator right to relocate Republican

indicators.note: the instruction is to move the Republican letter to a new spot, leaving the others in order

explanation.surface: An official is entitled to transfer a Republican to another post.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the usual abbreviation for Republican; only that letter moves, from third place to second.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefect is an administrator, as in the chief officer of a French department or a Roman official.

clue.text: Invented some fake news? Have a rest

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically as two words: told an untruth, and of one's own making

explanation.surface: Someone who has been spreading falsehoods is told to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LIED OWN: someone who lied made up their own story, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline on a bed or sofa for a while is to rest, the everyday phrasal verb.

clue.text: Kitty best seen from the rear

indicators.note: viewing from behind means reading the word from its back end

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: A cat looks its finest viewed from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitty and pot both mean the pool of money staked in a card game.

clue.text: Cleo dances wildly, beginning to enjoy her teenage years

indicators.note: dancing wildly suggests jumbled movement, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

explanation.surface: A girl called Cleo dances with abandon as she starts to enjoy being a teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescence is the period between childhood and adulthood, roughly the teens.

clue.text: Tax too much on small school?

parts.note: over in the sense of above, upon
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A question about whether a small school is being taxed excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks financial, but here it means to put strain on.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax a person or muscle is to make heavy demands on it; doing so excessively is to overstrain.

clue.text: Think matters over, as farm resident might?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ponder at length, an idiom
second meaning, literal: what a cow does, bringing up food to chew again

explanation.surface: A farmyard animal appears to be pondering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminants regurgitate and rechew their food, and the idiom borrows this for slow, repeated reflection.

clue.text: Royal favourite participating in public orgies

indicators.note: something participating in a group is found inside it, so the letters sit within the next words

explanation.surface: A royal favourite caught up in public debauchery, a tabloid scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept Pembroke Welsh corgis, her best-loved breed of dog.

clue.text: Swimmers once caught malaria, unfortunately

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Swimmers in the past fell ill with malaria, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers once' means creatures that used to swim: squid, now cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid served as food, so it consists of sea creatures that formerly swam.

clue.text: Article on Her Majesty's age

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another is attached after it, so the earlier-named piece goes second

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about how old the Queen is.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, which is one meaning of an age.

clue.text: Soviet hostage displaying spirit

indicators.note: displaying means putting on show, so the letters are visible inside the words

explanation.surface: A captive held by the Soviets shows great courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a community or era.

clue.text: Blessed everyone in house getting married

indicators.note: in tells us one word is put inside another

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A whole household feels lucky as someone gets married.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or sanctified, so it is a synonym of blessed.

clue.text: Lenten music strangely radiant

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Music played during Lent sounds oddly bright.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminescent means giving off light, which is what radiant also means.

clue.text: Wizard claiming space in household

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so one part grips the other inside

parts.note: an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A magician grabs some room at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link joining wordplay to definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ménage, from French, means the members of a household, as in ménage à trois.

clue.text: Moo, funny chap without any clothes

indicators.note: stripped of clothes means the outer covering is taken off, leaving the inside

parts.note: a clown is a comic performer

explanation.surface: The setter introduces himself as a naked comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Moo is the setter's pseudonym, so the clue doubles as a self-portrait; as a definition it is the sound a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's moo is called lowing, so to low is the verb, and the noun also names that sound.

clue.text: Crown's anger about end of deference

indicators.note: about means going around, so one part encircles the other
the end of a word is its final letter only

explanation.surface: The monarch's fury at a lack of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of laurel or flowers was worn on the head as a crown, as by victors in antiquity.

clue.text: Cabinet member I ignored in church

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a government minister sits in the cabinet

explanation.surface: A government minister is snubbed during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, such as York Minster.

clue.text: End of tipsy politician?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a word has two ends, so its end is its first letter or its last
second meaning: a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician's drunken spell comes to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The word tipsy has two ends, its first and last letters, so its 'end' is one letter or the other: T OR Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, so the answer names a politician.

clue.text: Sentence that will leave you hanging?

definitions.text: Sentence that will leave you hanging?

parts.words: Sentence that will leave you hanging?
parts.note: surface reading: a sentence with no ending, leaving a reader in suspense

parts.words: Sentence that will leave you hanging?
parts.note: setter's reading: a judge's sentence of death by the gallows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' looks grammatical and 'hanging' suggests suspense, but it is a court's death sentence, carried out with a noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A condemned prisoner given this sentence would literally be hanged, an old idiom for capital punishment.

clue.text: Drugs being used up, drink too much

indicators.note: in a down light, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: two drugs: E for ecstasy and pot for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone whose drugs have run out turns to heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is an old verb meaning to drink alcohol habitually and to excess.

clue.text: Federer's got it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the tennis player's first name
second meaning: radio-speak for message received

explanation.surface: A tennis fan cheers that the Swiss champion has won the point.
explanation.walkthrough: Federer's is short for Federer is, giving his forename.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio communication the reply meaning message understood is this word; it is also the given name of tennis great Federer.

clue.text: Dine with Trump when stoned? That would be unwise

indicators.note: someone stoned is in an altered, disordered state, so these letters get jumbled

explanation.surface: Having dinner with Donald Trump while high would be a poor decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking care or good judgement, a direct synonym of unwise.
